slides.headline: 6 AI PROMPTS YOUR BOSS USES BEFORE EVERY MEETING
slides.kicker: SAVE THESE BEFORE YOUR NEXT ONE

slides.headline: 1) KNOW MORE ABOUT THEM THAN THEY KNOW ABOUT YOU
slides.body: Executive briefing services charge $2,000 a month for this. "I'm meeting [name, title, company] tomorrow. Give me their biggest wins, pain points, and what they'll care about most"

slides.headline: 2) TURN THEIR WEBSITE INTO YOUR AMMUNITION
slides.body: A competitive analyst charges $200 an hour for this. "Here is [company]'s About page. What do they value most, what's their biggest weakness, and what language would impress them in a meeting?"

slides.headline: 3) PREDICT EVERY OBJECTION BEFORE IT'S RAISED
slides.body: A $50,000 deal dies from one objection nobody prepared for. "Here is my proposal. List the 5 strongest objections the other side will raise and write a calm one-sentence rebuttal for each"

slides.headline: 4) WRITE THE FOLLOW-UP BEFORE THE MEETING STARTS
slides.body: Write it before you walk in, send it 90 seconds after you leave. You look impossibly organized. "Draft a follow-up email for [topic]. Recap 3 key decisions and propose one clear next step"

slides.headline: 5) BUILD A ONE-PAGE CHEAT SHEET IN 30 SECONDS
slides.body: A consultant charges $300 an hour to build these. "Create a one-page meeting brief for [topic]. Include key facts, my 3 strongest talking points, and 2 questions that show I've done my homework"

slides.headline: 6) ASK THE ONE QUESTION THAT WINS THE ROOM
slides.body: One perfect question beats 30 minutes of talking. "I'm meeting [person, role] about [topic]. Give me one unexpected question that shows I understand their real problem, not just the surface one"

slides.headline: SAVE THIS FOR YOUR NEXT MEETING
slides.body: You'll want these prompts in your pocket when it counts. Save this post and follow @yaffeai for daily AI skills and news

caption:
Swipe to see the 6 AI prompts that win meetings before they even start 🎯

Research everyone in the room using AI, turn their own website into your ammunition, predict every objection before it's raised, write the follow-up before the meeting even starts, build a one-page cheat sheet in 30 seconds, and ask the one question that wins the entire room.

The gap between people who use AI to prepare and people who wing it is getting wider every week. The prepared ones aren't smarter, they just walk in knowing things nobody expects.
